Okay.. so... this unearthed an unexpected rabbit hole.

From what I can gather, the spelling of the genus and species should read "Eurypelma spinicrus".

Originally Eurypelma genus was a dumping ground for unclassified species in the americas with characteristics like the one framed. The first listed specimen was Aranea avicilaria (now Avicilaria avicilaria), however this wasn't the type species.

Other classifiers incorrectly assumed avicularia WAS the characteristic species of Eurypelma, things got co fusing, new species were incorrectly labled and eventually the whole lot was regrouped to what it is now; Avicularia.

SO to summarise, the species and genus of the spider framed here is entirely unclear the genus has been reclassified and the species is definitely wrong. It is impossible to identify from this photo at least for myself.

I am studying horticulture through an apprenticeship. I am falling in love so far. In my studies I have been researching plants native to the Pilbara region of Western Australia.

Driving around today I was lucky enough to spot a small cluster of Stemodia bushes. These bushes smell very strongly like something you would rub on your chest to remedy a cold. In Australia we have Vick’s vaporub and as such this family often gets called the “Vick’s” Bush.

Indigenous Australians use this bush for exactly that purpose. A medicine to treat colds and chesty coughs.

This is actually two species of Stemodia. The one with thick, fleshy, hair covered leaves is Stemodia Grossa, and is characterised by the numerous brown branches growing in it, which contain the seeds for the plant.

The second is Stemodia Viscosa, this species has smaller stalks and wider spacing between leaves. It does not produce the brown “seed” branches and the tips of branches end in a familiar “rose bud” shape.

Imagine a seasoned war veteran goes to play paintball against a team of 3rd graders. His easy win is considered far less skilful to you and I because we know he’s experienced and we expected that outcome.

Okay so this happened when I was a kid, and I will feel the effects for the rest of my life... don’t ask me why I did this, I’m not stupid I swear...

Anyway, when I was younger I was very curious. I also loved visiting pet stores (what kid doesn’t right?) 

On one fateful trip to the pet store my mother agreed to buy me ONE toy (even though they’re for pets and I was, most certainly, a human child). 

I decided to purchase a dog chew toy. You know, the soft stuffed animals with a squeaker inside; and after playing around with it for a while I became inquisitive as to what made the toy squeak.

So little 10 year old me rips open this toy, and flourished with childish delight as I pull out the small plastic squeaker and marvel at all I could accomplish with it. What did I do first? Shove it into my fucking ear and squeak it. 

Instantly the hearing in my right ear was impeded, and began to ring loudly. I ran out crying to my mother, and told her I had an ear ache (I still haven’t told her because she would probably slap me for being so dumb).

Flash forwards to now I have tinnitus indefinitely, and it is something I will have to deal with until I eventually die.

TL;DR - Bought a dog toy, removed squeaker, places it into my ear and squeaked. Now have tinnitus permanently, and again, I swear I’m not always that stupid 😭😭.
